editorial:
Imagine being a huge Hollywood star and having to go back to your small hometown to put on a local play just to help your girlfriend get a green card. That is exactly the mess you get into with Jeff Goldblum in this hilarious comedy. You will love watching him struggle through terrible rehearsals and deal with an agent who is losing his mind. The vibe is light, cozy, and full of that awkward charm Goldblum is known for. It feels like a warm hug of a movie where everything that can go wrong does go wrong, but in the funniest way possible.

What really makes this work is the chemistry between the cast and the funny tension of a big star trying to fit back into a small town. The pacing is snappy, though some of the side plots move a bit slow. If you enjoy stories about people trying to do things they are totally unqualified for, you need to see this. Since the colors of the town are so bright and nostalgic, you should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video if you can. Otherwise, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to spend a lazy Friday night.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head during the opening night of The Music Man. Despite all the mistakes and the chaos during rehearsals, the show actually becomes a huge hit because the audience loves the raw energy. Jeff manages to save his relationship and his fiancee finally gets her legal papers. He realizes that spending time with his old friends was more important than his fancy Hollywood image, and they all end the movie on a happy note.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves awkward humor and heartwarming stories about home.
